reason: Selected main-text sections provide a gated-versus-ungated contrast, explicit negative controls, and important limits on monitored evaluation and unavailable artifacts. A second proposal about retirement is inferred from the recorded lifecycle, not independently ablated.

candidates.title: Check a skill’s false triggers as well as its targeted fix
candidates.rule: For SEC-filing QA skill patches, require targeted improvement, preservation of protected correct answers, and no activation on declared out-of-scope negative controls before promotion.
candidates.passage: the ungated condition records larger gains on its candidates’ targeted sets but admits protected-case regressions.
candidates.finding: The full system has no recorded protected regressions in the in-house comparison; removing the protected gate admits three despite larger targeted gains. The promotion rule also includes false-trigger controls. Removing the gate alone does not isolate the separate contribution of every negative-control check.
models: Qwen3-Max answer judge; serving backbone not established in inspected sections
candidates.conditions: Skills declare applicability, injection points and false-trigger guards. Promotion compares the proposed registry with the current one using targeted cases, a protected suite and negative controls.
candidates.limitations: Gate confidence intervals on FinanceBench and FinDER include zero. The twelve-round monitoring set is observed repeatedly, routing and diagnosis also change, and artifacts and split manifests are incomplete. Labels are model-judged with author-group agreement checks, not independent financial-expert validation.
candidates.validation_test: Compare gated and ungated patches under the same budget. Measure false activation and protected regressions, then assess retained skills on a final financial-QA set not consulted during promotion.

candidates.title: Test retirement when one skill absorbs another
candidates.rule: When an evolved skill subsumes an older one, test removing the inactive duplicate and retain version history instead of growing the registry indefinitely.
candidates.passage: It retained four active skills from R5 to R12 while its static skill text shrank from 421 to 347 tokens.
candidates.finding: The reported registry consolidates versions and retires a dormant skill after its behavior is absorbed. This motivates a retirement check, but the study does not isolate consolidation as the cause of the observed quality improvement.
candidates.conditions: The system records activation, version replacement and removal tests while maintaining targeted and protected checks.
candidates.limitations: One evolving registry with concurrent routing and diagnosis changes. The marginal token cost of skill text is not separately measured. Inactivity alone does not prove redundancy, particularly for rare but important cases.
candidates.validation_test: Compare old and consolidated registries on protected, rare-trigger and out-of-scope cases. Retire the old version only if its required behavior remains covered; preserve a rollback path.

review_scope: Focused reading of abstract/introduction and selected main-text results, ablations and limitations; intervening sections, references and appendices were not comprehensively reviewed.
